scope_description.value: Replace existing broken steam boiler and all associated equipment and controls in Building 301. Install new high-efficiency gas-fired cast iron steam boiler (5.6 MMBH). Replace approximately 100 steam traps (65 thermostatic angle traps on radiators, 45 inverted bucket traps on ceiling-hung heaters). Provide boiler feed pumps with variable frequency drives, deaerator, expansion tank, chemical treatment unit, auto/manual blowdown. Provide DDC/BACnet control panel compatible with existing Niagara building automation system. Asbestos abatement required on approximately 66 existing steam trap locations. Modify electrical service as needed for new equipment. Building to remain occupied during construction.
scope_description.quote: Remove existing broken steam boiler, all associated equipment controls. Install new steam high efficiency boiler for building 301, A Permit to Construct (PTC) will be required from the Maryland Department of the Environment. Replace all steam traps, repair any steam, or water leaks.

taxonomy_notes.delivery_method: Construction task order is technically design-bid-build (BFA provided design BOD, NAVFAC issued construction RFP to MACC holders). BOD was authored by BFA as design support; construction was separately contracted via 8(a) MACC task order. 'design_bid_build' is the closest match.
taxonomy_notes.bfa_role: BFA authored the Basis of Design document (BFA Project #20-053) which served as the technical basis for the NAVFAC construction RFP. BFA's role appears to be engineering design/BOD author supporting NAVFAC's RFP development — effectively a specialty consultant on the design side. BFA did not hold the construction contract.
taxonomy_notes.award_type: RFP Basis for Award states 'lowest price' among 8(a) MACC holders per FAR 16.505. Closest vocab entry is 'lowest_price_technically_acceptable' though the document says 'lowest price' (price-only evaluation, not LPTA with technical threshold). Minor vocabulary gap noted.
taxonomy_notes.program_subtype: Building 301 at NAS Pax River is a support/utility building housing a boiler plant — mapped to military_maintenance as closest fit.
taxonomy_notes.project_status: BOD is Final Submittal dated December 2020; RFP was issued June 2020. Project is presumed complete given dates, but no closeout documentation available to confirm. Mapped 'complete' as best estimate.

conflict_flags.resolution_chosen: Both dates accepted as factually correct for their respective phases.
conflict_flags.rationale: The BOD Final Submittal date (December 2020) post-dates the RFP solicitation date (June 2020). This means the BOD was likely revised/finalized after the initial RFP was issued — the BOD may have been an RFP support document that went through multiple revisions. The timeline is plausible: RFP solicited June 2020, award ~August-September 2020, BOD finalized December 2020 as design documentation for the construction phase. No substantive data conflict.

claims.value: ~65 thermostatic angle traps + ~45 inverted bucket traps = ~110 traps

conflict_flags.resolution_chosen: BOD detailed breakdown (~110 total) is more specific; RFP '~100' is rounded estimate.
conflict_flags.rationale: The RFP description 'approximately 100 Steam Traps' is a rounded figure consistent with the BOD's more detailed breakdown of 65 + 45 = 110 traps. Minor discrepancy attributable to rounding in the RFP description vs. itemized BOD counts. No major conflict.

claims.value: Replace three (1) Steam boiler — apparent typo: '(1)' suggests one boiler
Install new high efficiency boiler for building 301 (singular)
BOD also references 'both boilers' and 'operate both boilers and corresponding pumps'

conflict_flags.resolution_chosen: One new boiler replacing one failed unit; BOD references 'both boilers' likely meaning new + existing standby or phased approach.
conflict_flags.rationale: The RFP text 'Replace three (1) Steam boiler' appears to be a formatting/typo artifact ('three' is likely extraneous). BOD consistently describes one new boiler. References to 'both boilers' in the BOD controls section may refer to the new boiler plus a retained or standby unit, or refer to lead/lag protocol for a future second boiler. Treated as one-boiler replacement for primary scope.
